user_questions.question: The price action already checks ownership, but against an accountId the agent supplies; verification is an email lookup (Get_Customer_Profile). (1) Should 'verified as' mean the Contact returned by Get_Customer_Profile, with the price action deriving the account from that Contact server-side (A), or add emailed code verification using the existing Send_Email_with_Verification_Code / Verify_Code flows (B)? (2) Scope: menu price action only, or all menu write actions? (3) On a mismatch: fail with an explicit error and no update, or something else?
user_questions.simulated_answer: The menu price action must verify the Menu Item belongs to a storefront on the verified contact's account; fail loudly otherwise. (A, price action only, explicit failure.)

user_questions.question: AgentUpdateMenuItemPriceActions also backs Update_Menu_Item_Price_179Kj000000oape in the active internal Merchant_Management_Agent, which has no Get_Customer_Profile action. (A) Enforce the verified-contact check in the shared class (employee agent price updates break); (B) keep the shared class unchanged and add a thin verified wrapper used only by the Merchant Support Agent (recommended); (C) make verifiedCustomerId optional in the shared class (weaker).
user_questions.simulated_answer: No preference; use your recommended default.

skill_friction: SKILL.md step 5 allows one more scope message when a new blocking fork appears later, but does not say whether it must be sent before or after R/T; here the shared-class fork (active employee agent uses the same Apex class) surfaced only from my own org queries after T, forcing an I re-send after R and T were already based on the superseded inventory. The skill does not say whether R/T must be re-sent after a post-T redesign.

org-verification.md has no guidance for Agentforce metadata: GenAiPlannerDefinition has no Metadata column, BotDefinition is standard-API only, and planner/topic/action links must be traced via GenAiPlannerFunctionDef and GenAiPluginFunctionDef. Also no guidance on whether topic-local actions (suffixed DeveloperNames) deploy as GenAiFunction or inside GenAiPlannerBundle, which forced a Conditional row.
AskCoworker D1/D2/R/T repeatedly cited 'prior session' facts; the rule to verify them is clear but costs many queries; no guidance on how many are required when they are not design-relevant.

The requirement's premise ('agent is updating prices for any merchant') is partly contradicted (ownership check already exists; bot user lacks Price__c Edit FLS). Step 5's 'premise is false' default (zero-change spec) does not fit a partly-false premise where the real gap is trust in an input; had to judge this myself.

Rule 4 (drop behavior nobody asked for) vs AskCoworker's 'blocking' permission grant: the skill says judge blocking yourself and grants are open decisions, which worked, but it is unclear whether a responsibility's allow-path failing due to existing missing FLS counts as 'cannot deliver a responsibility end to end' requiring a scope question.
